job_ceiling.warning: batch job bound 129720s (options.timeout_s 1800s x 72 units + 120s; a conservative fully-serial upper bound, not a runtime estimate) exceeds the fleet's whole-job ceiling of 3600s (max_job_seconds from fleet_config); a job still running at the ceiling is killed and every unit is reported batch_job_timeout. Set request.remote.hosts to at least 72 to run one job per shard of at most 1 units, each within the ceiling

environment.timeout_preflight_warning: options.timeout_s (1800s) looks implausible for a tran analysis with ~1.02e+05 timepoints (2p step, 204.812n window) -- even 50 timepoints/s (a generous floor, not a real engine-rate estimate) would need 2.05e+03s per corner. This is only a coarse, advisory pre-grid heuristic -- it does not block the sweep, and a plausible-looking budget can still turn out to be too short in practice.
